anomalies.observed: On the I2C Sensors sheet, the Atlas Scientific EZO-pH and EZO-EC circuits have their PGND pins tied to ordinary GND symbols, while the isolated ground nets /GNDISO_pH and /GNDISO_EC are connected only to ADM3260 pin 20 and the M2/M3 GND pins.
anomalies.expected: The pH and EC wet-chemistry channels are intended to be galvanically isolated, with their probe/circuit grounds on the isolated domains /GNDISO_pH and /GNDISO_EC and not tied to the main GND domain.

evidence.quote: M2 ATLAS_EZO-pH ... PGND ... GND; M3 ATLAS_EZO_EC ... PGND ... GND; /GNDISO_pH, /GNDISO_EC
each with a dedicated isolated supply (/V_pH, /V_EC) and isolated ground (/GNDISO_pH, /GNDISO_EC)
galvanically separate from the main +3V3/+5V/+24V domains.

anomalies.impact: Tying the probe ground PGND to main GND defeats the purpose of the isolated pH/EC channels: it creates a ground-loop path through the nutrient solution, can corrupt pH/EC readings, and may expose the isolated ADM3260 domain to non-isolated ground currents.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears to contain an isolation fault: the pH and EC probe grounds (M2/M3 PGND) are connected to the non-isolated GND net, contradicting the intended galvanically isolated pH/EC domains.
